subject: Hosted evaluation: routing, endpoints, and quickstart questions
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@octanepay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up — hosted evaluation next steps & routing Qs

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really appreciate the clarity on OctanePay's checkout flows. Per our conversation, it sounds like you're leaning toward trying Redwood's Hosted API first so you can move quickly, but we wanted to confirm a few deployment and routing details before we spin up a sandbox: 

High-level recap from our side:
- Goal: conversational customer support + payment intent summarization in checkout (short prompts, lots of transactions).
- Preferred path: Hosted API evaluation (fast onramp) with the option to migrate to Dedicated if you need sustained throughput or VPC isolation.

A few quick questions that will determine the endpoint mapping and rate slice we provision for your trial: 
1) Peak concurrency / QPS: what were the highest requests-per-second numbers you saw in the busiest minute (or an estimate)?
2) Typical request length: average token size for prompts/responses (short — <150 tokens — or long)?
3) Latency SLO target for inference (p50/p95) you need to hit in production?
4) Data residency or regulatory needs (PCI scope, PII handling, desire for Private/VPC)?
5) Do you expect to use embeddings or reranking in the pilot, or only generation?

Suggested quickstart mapping we recommend for hosted evaluation: 
- inference.redwood.io/v1/generate -> main checkout/chat endpoint (capped prefix + KV cache)
- inference.redwood.io/v1/embeddings -> embeddings only (separate rate slice)
- Canary endpoint -> for A/B canary traffic during rollouts

I've attached our quickstart checklist (redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf) and the hosted onramp playbook (hosted-onramp-playbook.md) so your infra and security teams can skim the ops requirements.

Proposed next steps:
- Can you reply with answers to the five short questions above?
- If hosted looks good, let's schedule a 30-minute ops sync (here's a slot picker: https://calendly.com/redwood/ops-sync-30m).

If some of this needs to be kept private to your security team, feel free to loop them in or forward the attachments.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com

From: Claire Huang <claire@octanepay.com>

Cc: Ravi Kapoor <ravi.kapoor@octanepay.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — hosted evaluation next steps & routing Qs

Chloe —

Thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Answering your questions below (short answers to move fast):

1) Peak concurrency / QPS: ~120 QPS sustained for a 90s window during promotions; typical steady-state is 25–40 QPS.
2) Typical request length: short prompts, average ~80 tokens in/out.
3) Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms would be ideal for checkout UX, p50 <= 120ms.
4) Data residency / PCI: Payments are in PCI scope; we tokenize card data earlier in the flow and only send non-sensitive text to models. Our security team will need SOC2 / audit logs and an assurance we can opt into a Private deployment if required.
5) Embeddings/reranking: We will run tiny reranking for fraud signals (low volume) in parallel — so embeddings endpoint would be used but lower QPS.

Additional questions from our side:
- Can Hosted support burst capacity above the baseline limit for sale spikes? How do you handle sudden 3x traffic surges?
- Is KV/prefix caching applied automatically or config-based per endpoint?
- Cost estimates: rough ballpark for 120 QPS short prompts for a one-week pilot?

If it helps, I can loop in our security lead (Ravi) on the next thread to handle SOC2 artifacts. We're flexible on a Monday ops sync if that works for you.

Thanks,
Claire
Head of Product
OctanePay
claire@octanepay.com
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@octanepay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — hosted evaluation next steps & routing Qs

Claire — really helpful, thanks for the granular numbers. A couple quick clarifications and what we'll provision for the pilot: 

Short answers to your questions:
- Burst capacity: Hosted supports automatic short-term bursting using pooled capacity and we offer an optional burst reservation for promotional windows. For the pilot we'll provision a slice sized for 150 QPS burst with a steady-rate target of 40 QPS. If you expect repeated sustained >500 QPS, we recommend Dedicated.
- KV/prefix caching: caching is enabled by default for repeat prefixes; we can also configure explicit TTLs per endpoint if you want stronger caching behavior.
- Cost ballpark (very approximate for planning): for short prompts at 120 QPS over 1 week (24/7 high), expect a hosted pilot range of $6k–$12k depending on model choice and caching effectiveness. We'll produce a tighter estimate after we know model selection.

Proposed endpoint mapping for the pilot (what we'll create in the sandbox):
- /v1/generate (model: open-variant recommended for evaluation) — primary checkout calls, rate slice: steady 40 QPS, burst to 150 QPS
- /v1/embeddings (model: small embed) — separate slice, steady 2–5 QPS
- /v1/canary (same model as generate) — kept at <5% of traffic for rollout testing

Security/artifacts: Jordan and Marissa will share SOC2 audit artifacts and sample audit logs via a secured drive link for Ravi to review. If OctanePay needs VPC or on-prem for PCI compliance, we can start a parallel Private deployment discussion, but for the pilot hosted should be fine since card data is already tokenized upstream.

Action items: 
1) Claire: confirm model preference (open-variant or specific LLM) and Monday ops window that works for you.
2) Jordan/Marissa: I'll coordinate SOC2 artifacts and the sandbox provisioning plan.
3) I'll schedule the Monday 30m ops sync — sending a Calendly link below.

Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/ops-sync-30m

Quick note on observability: we'll enable per-route token and latency traces during the pilot so you can see p50/p95 by client. That makes it easier to tune batching and caching.

Best,
Chloe

Redwood Inference
